page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a big data instance family configuration engineered specifically for distributed storage and processing environments. Operating on KVM virtualization with 64-bit x86 architecture, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. With 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of memory, it provides a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation, allowing reliable multi-threaded execution for data processing frameworks.

The central hardware capability of the ecs.d1.6xlarge is its bundled storage architecture, which includes 70,866 GB of local mechanical HDD capacity. Unlike instances that rely on network-attached storage or low-capacity solid-state drives, this dense hard disk setup maximizes volumetric storage per compute node. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth pipe, ensuring steady inter-node cluster replication. The instance does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural perspective, relying on mechanical hard drives presents a clear tradeoff: sequential read and write throughput across large data volumes is prioritized over low-latency random input/output operations. This design provides economical storage density relative to solid-state alternatives. The ecs.d1.6xlarge is suitable for distributed analytics, Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) nodes, large-scale MapReduce jobs, Apache Spark batch tasks, and centralized log repositories.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.6xlarge is a big data instance designed for storage-intensive distributed workloads. Built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, delivering 24 dedicated vCPUs. The server pairs this processing core count with 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A defining architectural element is the inclusion of 70,866 GB of local HDD storage, providing substantial dense capacity directly on the host without relying exclusively on networked block volumes. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network interface and operates without discrete GPUs. With an emphasis on capacity density over random I/O speed, this hardware profile offers favorable cost efficiency for massive sequential storage pipelines. It is suited for MapReduce frameworks, Apache Hadoop clusters, distributed data warehousing, and log collection systems.
